name: antepartum hemorrhage overview
title: Bleeding in the second or third trimester: after the mother and fetus are assessed and non-obstetric sources and labour are ruled out, pain and whose blood it is separate placental abruption (edge or concealed), placenta previa, the placenta accreta spectrum and vasa previa; each column gives presentation, numbered investigations and treatment in order, and a panel sets delivery by gestation

nodes.title: Bleeding in the 2nd or 3rd trimester: is it PAINFUL, and WHOSE blood is it?
lines: every one: airway, breathing, circulation for mom (oxygen + intravenous access if unstable) · non-stress test (NST) for the fetus
stat: complete blood count · international normalized ratio (INR), partial thromboplastin time (PTT), FIBRINOGEN · creatinine · group and screen
rule out first: non-obstetric (hemorrhoids, varices, bladder infection, stones → treat the cause) and LABOUR (a dilating cervix bleeds: 'show')

nodes.title: PAINFUL, tender uterus
lines: maternal blood

nodes.title: PAINLESS: where is the placenta?
lines: maternal blood · placental site from the anatomy scan

nodes.title: Small bleed, FETAL DISTRESS
lines: the blood is the FETUS's

nodes.title: Placental abruption
lines: premature separation of the placenta from the uterus
most at 35–38 weeks, any gestation

nodes.title: Placenta previa
lines: implanted over, or within 2 cm of, the internal os
complete: covers it · marginal: within 2 cm

nodes.title: Placenta accreta spectrum
lines: accreta · increta · percreta
placenta INVADES the uterine wall

nodes.title: Vasa previa
lines: unprotected FETAL vessels cross the cervix or lie within 2 cm

nodes.title: Painful active bleeding
lines: • tender, sometimes RIGID uterus
• 'unrelenting contractions'

nodes.title: At the EDGE (most)
lines: bleeds out · mild–moderate pain

nodes.title: CONCEALED
lines: NO bleeding · severe pain · fetal distress

nodes.title: PAINLESS bleeding, mild or severe
lines: • sentinel bleed at 26–28 weeks
• fetus stable unless the mother is not

nodes.title: Bleeding the uterus cannot control
lines: myometrium cannot contract over the invaded site

nodes.title: Small bleed, FETAL DISTRESS
lines: a tiny volume is a lot of the fetus's blood

nodes.title: Known from the scan?
lines: • type 1: velamentous cord insertion
• type 2: succenturiate (extra) lobe

nodes.title: 1 · A diagnosis of EXCLUSION
lines: once the other sources are ruled out

nodes.title: 2 · Trauma or fetal distress: Kleihauer-Betke
lines: fetal blood in HER circulation

nodes.title: 1 · Ultrasound: placenta to the os
lines: found at the 18–20 week scan; many move clear by the 3rd trimester

nodes.title: ANY cervical change can start a SUDDEN, SEVERE bleed
1 · Ask: previous cesarean or uterine surgery?
lines: the scar lacks a full endometrial cover

nodes.title: 1 · Apt test
lines: fetal blood in the VAGINAL bleed

nodes.title: Blood irritates the myometrium
lines: • may go into LABOUR
• may rupture the membranes

nodes.title: Deliver or wait by gestation
lines: see the panel ↓

nodes.title: 1 · Severe bleed: transfuse + clotting factors
lines: no myometrium to clamp the vessels: shock, coagulopathy, hysterectomy

nodes.title: Marginal, > 1 cm from the os
lines: vaginal birth in select cases

nodes.title: Almost always HYSTERECTOMY
lines: unless the invasion is very focal

nodes.title: Fetal status drives delivery
lines: see the panel ↓

panels.title: Every bleed: mother and fetus, then GESTATION decides
items: ≥ 35–36 weeks: DELIVER · induction if mother and fetus are reassuring, cesarean section if not

PRETERM + active bleed: birthing unit, continuous fetal monitoring · steroids + magnesium sulfate (see the PRETERM LABOUR chart) · neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) or tertiary consult if < 28–32 weeks · bloods every 4–6 h
PRETERM, stable, bleeding settled: antenatal ward · NST, growth + placental ultrasound, periodic bloods
the danger: CONSUMPTIVE COAGULOPATHY · the placental bed's huge flow uses up platelets and clotting factors
